runs.question: What fine does OMB M-25-21 set for an agency that misses its AI strategy deadline?

answer.text:
OM M-25-21 does not set a fine for an agency that misses its AI strategy deadline. I searched the memo for fines, penalties, and monetary consequences, and found none.

What the memo does say about the deadline: each CFO Act agency must develop an AI Strategy for identifying and removing barriers to their responsible use of AI and for achieving enterprise-wide improvements in the maturity of their applications, and that work is due within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum. The strategies must also be made public, and the memo's consolidated action table lists this as a requirement for each CFO Act agency. The footnote on scope says the requirement applies to CFO Act agencies except for the Department of Defense, and does not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community.

The memo does not describe what happens if the deadline is missed. The closest enforcement language concerns high-impact AI, not the strategy. For that category, agencies must have a plan to discontinue its use until actions are taken to achieve compliance with this memorandum. That is an operational consequence, not a fine.

If you need the consequences of a missed deadline, check the statutes the memo cites, such as the AI in Government Act of 2020 and the Advancing American AI Act, or ask OMB directly. I did not find that information in the documents provided.

Passage concerns high-impact AI when not performing appropriately, not the strategy deadline or any strategy-related discontinuation plan; it is a different requirement.

citations.title: OMB M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust, April 2025, page 5
citations.cited_text: Developing Agency AI Strategies Within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum, each CFO Act agency must develop an AI Strategy for identifying and removing barriers to their responsible use of AI and for achieving enterprise-wide improvements in the maturity of their applications.

citations.title: OMB M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust, April 2025, page 6
citations.cited_text: 9 Consistent with sections 7225(d) and 7228 of the Advancing American AI Act, this requirement applies to CFO Act agencies except for the Department of Defense, and does not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community, as defined in 50 U.S.C. § 3003(4). Information that would be protected from release ifrequested under 5 U.S.C. § 552 need not be included in the strategy.

citations.title: OMB M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust, April 2025, page 3
citations.cited_text: When the high-impact AI is not performing at an appropriate level, agencies must have a plan to discontinue its use until actions are taken to achieve compliance with this memorandum. If proper risk mitigation is not possible, agencies must cease the use of the AI.

checks.reason: Passage states CFO Act agencies must develop an AI Strategy for identifying and removing barriers and enterprise-wide maturity improvements.
Passage states the strategy must be developed within 180 days of the memorandum's issuance.
Footnote says the requirement applies to CFO Act agencies except DoD and does not apply to Intelligence Community elements.
Passage concerns high-impact AI when not performing appropriately, not the strategy deadline or any strategy-related discontinuation plan; it is a different requirement.
